alignments.note: Construct noun with a supplied *the*, no article morpheme present (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the *of* of the chain (rule 19); discontinuous around the possessive (rule 25).
Preposition and interrogative fused into the single word *whereto* (rule 30), headed on the interrogative, which carries the lexeme.
*should it profit* is a wholly supplied lexical verb with its dummy subject; the Hebrew clause has no verb at all (rule 20).
Dative לְ left with no English word by the recasting *profit me* (rule 40).
Preposition עַל → *in* in the ASV's relative recasting.

The ASV recasts this suffix's clause as a relative clause and supplies the lexical noun *Men* naming its referent for the relative to modify; both words realize the suffix in one unit, discontinuous around the preposition's own *in* (rules 18 and 25), and neither is `added`. Head on the noun carrying the referent, as JOB.30.13 heads *men that* on *men*; heading on the relative *whom* was the competing reading and is named here under rule 8.
*ripe age* for כֶּלַח; *age* alone is any age, so the head falls on the distinguishing word (rule 31). Reading the head on *age* was available and is named here under rule 8.

review_notes: Reconciliation with JOB.30.13: *Men* is no longer `added`. The same construction stands in both verses — a 3mp suffix whose clause the ASV recasts as a relative clause with a supplied antecedent noun — and rule 18 gives the whole expression to the suffix. Rule 17's supplied-subject sentence governs a noun supplied as the subject of a finite verb; *Men* is the antecedent of *whom*, and the clause's subject is *ripe age*.
*should it profit* is treated as a supplied lexical verb rather than a construction-supplied copula, since *profit* predicates an event the Hebrew never writes (rule 20).
The margin's *Or, vigor* was read and set aside; the printed *ripe age* is what is aligned (rule 38).
